History perturbations can reveal model dependence, but recommendation changes alone do not establish interest-specific reliance. CauseRec distinguishes indispensable versus dispensable item/interest concepts and trains representations to respond differently to their replacement; this provides motivation, rather than proof of a matched-control diagnostic. [CauseRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.05261). Rank List Sensitivity research finds substantial instability even after random interaction perturbations during training, reinforcing the need to measure generic corruption effects; that setting differs from masking histories at fixed-model inference. [RLS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12686).

Proposed reproducible diagnostic—not an established protocol verified in these sources: freeze weights and define interest groups from public histories and title/description similarity. Compare masking an interest group with repeated random masks from the same user, matching mask size, recency/position bins, training-only item-popularity bins, and repeated-item frequency where feasible. Predeclare bins, matching tolerances, seeds, and unmatched-case handling. Use identical masking and positional treatment for targeted and control interventions; separately test deletion/repacking because it changes sequence positions. Report matching balance and coverage. An excess effect supports model dependence on the operationalized interest beyond these measured corruption factors, without identifying real-world causal preferences.

Keep the original target fixed. Report rank deterioration Δr = r_masked − r_original, top-10 exit rate conditional on original inclusion, and list overlap |Top10_original ∩ Top10_masked|/10; Jaccard@10 and rank-biased overlap provide complementary list measures. [RLS](https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~srijan/pubs/CASPER-sejoon-CIKM-2022.pdf). Subtract each user’s mean matched-control effect from the targeted effect, bootstrap users for uncertainty, and macro-average categories. Keep candidates, exclusions, and tie-breaking fixed. Treat these as diagnostics alongside the unchanged validation HR@10 selection metric.
